question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. 2.
Statement
Some Deltas are Beaches.
All Deltas are cushions
Conclusions:
I. Some Beaches are cushions.
II. Some cushions is Deltas.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: Some Delta is both Beach and Cushion because Some Delta are Beaches and all Deltas are Cushions. Both existential conclusions follow.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. 3.
Statement
Some Apple are Banana.
No Banana is Date
Conclusions:
I. Some Apple are not Date.
II. Some Date are not Apple.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: The Some Apple-Banana overlap lies outside Date because no Banana is Date, so conclusion I follows. No existence relation forces Date and Apple apart; II does not follow.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. 4.
Statements:
Some Cat are Lion.
Some Cat is Bat.
Conclusions:
I. Some Bat are Lion.
II. No Bat are Lion.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: The two Cat overlaps may coincide or be disjoint. Therefore either some Bat is Lion or no Bat is Lion must hold as the complementary pair; option C.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. 5.
Statement
Some Pens are Pencil.
Some Pens are not Brush.
Conclusions:
I. Some Pencils are Pens.
II. Some Pencils are not Brush.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: Some Pens are Pencils directly gives Some Pencils are Pens. The separate Some Pens not Brush may be a different instance, so conclusion II does not follow.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. 6.
Statement
All Crows are Black.
All Black are Deer.
Conclusions:
I. All Deer are Black.
II. All Crows are Deer.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: Crow is a subset of Black, and Black a subset of Deer, so all Crows are Deer. The reverse universal is not implied.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. Q.9
Statements:
Some hero are singers.
All the singers are dancers.
Conclusions:
1. Some hero are dancers.
2. No singer is hero.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: Some Heroes are Singers and all Singers are Dancers, so some Heroes are Dancers. The stated overlap rules out the universal negative conclusion.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. Q.10 Statements:
All  piano are harmoniums.
All harmoniums are flutes.
Conclusions:
1. All flutes are harmoniums.
2. All piano are flutes.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: Piano ⊆ Harmonium ⊆ Flute proves all Pianos are Flutes; it does not prove all Flutes are Harmoniums.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. Q.11 Statements:
Some banana are yellow.
Some apple are banana.
Conclusions:
1. Some apple are yellow.
2. No apple is  yellow.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: The two existential premises need not concern the same Banana. Conclusions Some Apple are Yellow and No Apple is Yellow are complementary, so either-or holds.

question_text:
Syllogism, Level I. Q.12.  Statements:
Some boys are girls.
All the girls are students.
Conclusions:
1. All the students are girls.
2. Some boys are students.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

explanation: Some Boys are Girls and all Girls are Students, so that nonempty overlap is also Boys-Students. The universal reverse conclusion does not follow.
